A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ModTrack and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably across the revised layout and expanded supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original tracking results on WildTrack, MultiviewX, and RadarScenes, together with oracle experiments, matching-mode ablations, sensor-dropout tests, sensitivity analyses, and uncertainty calibration.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds component ablations, a vanilla GM-PHD comparison, longer-sequence evaluation, and additional radar-perception results.

M1.justification: Appendix K adds a tested MLP radar-perception variant alongside the previously reported Doppler and oracle front ends, although its architecture is unspecified. The analytical tracking core, covariance propagation, fusion equations, and identity-assignment and lifecycle procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate pedestrian tracking on WildTrack and MultiviewX and automotive radar tracking on RadarScenes. The additional experiments retain these datasets and modalities. Evaluating all 400 existing WildTrack frames changes the sequence length and evaluation protocol, without introducing a new dataset or population.

E2.justification: v3 adds vanilla GM-PHD comparisons on both camera datasets in Table 10 and adds MOT and CA-Net to the RadarScenes comparison in Table 4. Appendix C also adds a reported runtime comparison with MCBLT, previously an accuracy comparator only. These additions substantially expand comparisons relevant to the filtering core and radar performance; Table 1's comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: The original splits, training settings, and evaluation thresholds are retained. Appendix I adds inference across all 400 WildTrack frames using perception trained on the original 90/10 split, explicitly including training frames. New diagnostics specify single-component substitutions and a MultiviewX gate sweep; v3 also reports identity-switch counts and radar GOSPA. These extend the evaluation protocol without replacing the original experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds isolated tests of covariance-aware clustering, propagated covariance, and precision-weighted fusion. Section 4.4 adds a MultiviewX gate sweep measuring missed clusters versus merge errors. Appendices I-K add longer-sequence behavior, comparison with vanilla GM-PHD to assess the practical consequences of departing from formal PHD filtering, and an MLP radar-perception diagnostic. These substantially extend the existing matching-mode, dropout, sensitivity, and calibration analyses.

E5.justification: Camera-subset means and standard deviations, runtime uncertainty, and the NEES confidence-interval and coverage procedures are retained. No new repeated-run counts, random-seed reporting, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation practices are introduced. The deterministic RANSAC description concerns algorithm execution rather than repeated-run statistical estimation.

E6.justification: The original camera scores, dropout results, runtime measurements, and calibration statistics remain unchanged. New Table 9 reports IDF1/MOTA of 92.8/90.8 for RANSAC clustering, 95.0/90.7 for fixed covariance, and 93.0/89.5 for mean fusion, against 95.5/91.4. Table 10 adds vanilla-filter results and identity-switch counts; additional radar scores and the 400-frame results further expand the evidence. Table 10 reports ModTrack's MultiviewX IDF1 as 85.2, whereas retained Tables 1-2 report 86.2, with no explanation establishing a comparable-setting performance change.

T1.justification: The projection derivations, covariance flooring, fusion equations, filtering equations, and calibration mathematics are retained. Renaming Rdepth to Rindep is not a mathematical change. Appendix J explains departures from formal RFS/PHD guarantees and evaluates them empirically, without introducing a new theorem, proof, or revised recursion.

C1.justification: The abstract, three principal contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about modular tracking, traceable uncertainty, sensor flexibility, and competitive accuracy. The introduction adds an explicit assertion that the modifications to GM-PHD improve identity consistency while preserving state-estimation accuracy, modestly extending the claimed validation of the heuristic backend.

C2.justification: v3 develops several substantive interpretations and qualifications. Section 4.4 diagnoses the MultiviewX gap as a structural missed-cluster/merge tradeoff rather than merely crowding-related ambiguity. Section 3.3 explains the overlapping-camera rationale for singleton rejection and the radar exception. Appendix J explicitly states that component weights lose their expected-target-mass interpretation. Appendix I additionally claims no compounding tracking error from the longer-sequence experiment, despite its acknowledged training-data overlap.

D1.justification: Appendix L newly supplies a code-availability statement and repository address. Appendix H documents the deterministic consensus-clustering implementation, fixed covariance, and averaging substitutions, while Section 3.3 discloses radar singleton handling. The existing training recipes, hardware, and hyperparameter tables are retained. The added MLP experiment lacks architecture and training details.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Mahler's foundational PHD work, Marcuzzi et al.'s CA-Net work, and Weng et al.'s tracking baseline. The introduction refines its criticism of earlier multi-view RFS trackers toward missing covariance propagation across the pipeline. The broader related-work organization and positioning between learned tracking and RFS filtering remain intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes comprise localized clarifications, revised subsection labeling, an explicit supplementary-material heading, new Appendices H-L, and expanded author, affiliation, keyword, and acknowledgement text. The revision does not extensively rewrite the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v3 comprehensively reformats the document with narrower text blocks, running headers, and resized and redistributed figures and tables. Table 4 gains comparator rows and a GOSPA column, and Tables 9-10 are added. Table 7 moves to the final page. The underlying images for Figures 1-14 are unchanged, so their relocation and scaling are presentation changes.

improvement.justification: The component ablations and vanilla GM-PHD comparison provide more direct evidence for design choices that v1 principally supported through broader performance and sensitivity tests. The code-access statement and clearer limitations also help. These gains are moderated by the unexplained 85.2 versus 86.2 MultiviewX IDF1 discrepancy, sparse details for new experiments, and a long-sequence stability claim supported only by aggregate results with intentional training-data overlap. The evidence supports a limited overall improvement.
